name: WD-40
imitates: A tiny midge or baetis emerger with a mallard-fiber tail and wing case; a tailwater favorite when fish are keyed on small emergers.
recipe: Curved nymph/emerger hook, #16 shown (Mouche 8471), usually tied smaller

steps.text: Seat a small curved hook in the vise with the eye straight so the whip finish is easy later.
Start the thread about a quarter shank length behind the eye and wrap forward a few turns to lock it.
Align the tips of a small clump of mallard fibers and tie it in on top of the shank with the tips pointing back, so the tail ends up about half a shank long.
Wrap the thread back down the bend, keeping the mallard on top, until the tail sits at the right length.
Flatten the thread and wrap forward in touching turns to build a smooth tapered body, ending just behind the eye.
Dub a thin, short noodle and wrap it back toward the body to cover about the front third of the shank.
Pull the forward-pointing mallard fibers back over the thorax as a wing case, tie them down and trim the excess.
Wrap over the cut ends to tidy them, then whip finish behind the thorax and cut the thread. The finished fly.
